source.title: The Geometry of Alignment Collapse: When Fine-Tuning Breaks Safety
source.authors: Max Springer; Chung Peng Lee; Blossom Metevier; Jane Castleman; Bohdan Turbal; Hayoung Jung; Zeyu Shen; Aleksandra Korolova

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present. Some table extraction is imperfect for the no-fine-tuning baseline values.
record.tranche_reason: It fine-tunes aligned chat models and evaluates harmfulness afterward, bearing on safety degradation from fine-tuning, but uses a harmfulness score rather than the original refusal/compliance measure.
record.gate_note: The paper also reports theoretical results and an overlap-score analysis. The overlap-score figures are not harmful-behaviour measures; cited results from other studies are not this study's results. It does not measure response-position KL, test compliant prefills or decoding changes, or test safety after a method designed to deepen it.
record.test_reason: The study fine-tunes two aligned instruct models on Pure Bad (100 harmful examples) and on benign data (SamSum, random Alpaca, random GSM8K, gradient-selected Alpaca Top 100). It scores harmfulness on a 1–5 LLM-judge Harmfulness Score against a no-fine-tuning baseline. This is the same kind of measure and datasets as Qi et al., though with a different judge (Gemini-2.5-Flash), benchmark (AdvBench) and models. The rest of the paper is theory (Alignment Instability Condition, quartic scaling) plus Fisher-spectrum and overlap-score analyses that do not measure the behaviour.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim that all fine-tuning raises harmfulness, and that seemingly benign data reaches harmful-data HS levels. Their own Table 1 contradicts the first claim for LLaMA-3.2-3B LoRA on SamSum and GSM8K (1.10 vs 1.11). They claim the Overlap Score predicts risk under full FT but concede it does not under LoRA. Their core contribution is theoretical: alignment loss grows as t^4 via curvature coupling, so first-order defenses are insufficient.
record.recipe_differences: Uses fine-tuning on several benign, seemingly benign, and harmful datasets and evaluates with Gemini-2.5-Flash harmfulness scores on AdvBench. It does not reproduce the original refusal-rate recipe or test first-token concentration.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported harmfulness scores vary by dataset, model, and fine-tuning method. The authors also state that the overlap-score to harmfulness relationship is not clear for LoRA.

fits_no_version.finding: Projected block-wise Fisher information on 100 BeaverTails safe completions shows sharp low-rank eigenvalue decay in both models (Fig. 2, Fig. 5).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-relevant likelihood curvature is concentrated in a low-rank weight-space subspace. This is a curvature measure with no causal ablation or non-safety control.

fits_no_version.finding: The Overlap Score of fine-tuning updates with the Fisher subspace separates seemingly benign and Pure Bad from benign data under full FT. It fails for Alpaca Top 100 and shows no clear relation to HS under LoRA (Fig. 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Geometric overlap of updates with a safety Fisher subspace predicts post-fine-tuning harmfulness.

record.problems: Only two models are tested. Harmfulness is evaluated by one stated judge on a 1–5 scale, with no uncertainty reported. The supplied table extraction leaves the numeric no-fine-tuning baseline unclear. FIM eigenvalue results are presented in figures without numeric values. The paper notes that its overlap-score relation is unclear for LoRA.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant reported results were left out. Cited results from prior papers, theoretical claims without empirical measurements, and overlap-score plots that do not report the harmfulness behaviour itself were not entered as rows.

untested.parts: Compliance or refusal rates; how few examples suffice (only 100 tested); trajectory over training steps.
Compliance rates; dose or step dynamics; models beyond two small instruct models.
Per-token KL by response position; not measured.
Prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes; not tested.
Causal localization (pruning, ablation or rank removal of safety weights); only Fisher spectra measured.
Why safety is shallow across token positions; the paper's geometric theory concerns parameter drift, not token depth.

missing.what: HS for Risky Financial Advice (Qwen 3.94/3.78, LLaMA 4.71/3.82) and Bad Medical Advice (Qwen 3.92/3.86, LLaMA 2.46/3.65), LoRA/full. These are narrow misaligned-advice data, not benign; mapping is unclear (nearest V1).
No-fine-tuning baseline HS values (Qwen 1.24, LLaMA 1.11) are readable in Table 1 and should replace 'unclear' in every row.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche raised to T1: Qi et al. also use a 1–5 LLM-judge Harmfulness Score with Pure Bad and Alpaca, so the measure is not a departure. The judge, benchmark and models differ. The study tests only two small models, uses one judge, reports no seeds or uncertainty, and includes no capability check. V5 rows were unlinked because Fisher spectra do not show safety behaviour carried by few weights. Spiked spectra are also generic to neural nets, and no non-safety control is shown. Alpaca Top 100 was selected on LLaMA-2-7B-chat, so its transfer failure on LLaMA-3.2 LoRA is informative for V2's carefully chosen data.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests harmful fine-tuning with 100 Pure Bad examples, but does not report a harmful-compliance rate or establish that refusal is removed almost entirely.

It reports harmfulness scores after benign and gradient-selected benign fine-tuning, not a refusal or compliance rate; the numeric no-fine-tuning comparison is unclear in the supplied table extraction.
Per-token KL divergence by response position.
Compliant prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
The paper measures low-rank FIM structure, but does not ablate or edit a small set of weights or ranks to test whether they causally carry safety behaviour.
Whether data or a training objective causes safety behaviour to be shallow across response positions.
Training that spreads safety beyond early response tokens and its durability.
